chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Faraj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I asked him, 'Can a man send forward his tent and his luggage before the departure?' So he said: 'No, does he not fear that the one who sends forward his luggage that Allah the Exalted may withhold him?' He said: 'But he can leave behind whatever he desires, [provided he] does not enter it into Makkah.' I said, 'So if I hasten due to forgetfulness, fulfilling my rituals, and I quicken with it, beginning and the freeing [from Ihram]?' So he said: 'There is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sending forward luggage before the Hajj departure?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic preference for delaying the departure from Mina to ensure the completion of all rituals, warning that premature removal of luggage might lead to being 'held back' by Allah if essential rites are missed. It distinguishes between intentional haste and forgetfulness, offering leniency for the latter, which reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing ritual precision with divine mercy. The discussion underscores the theological concept that the timing of Hajj acts is not merely procedural but spiritually significant, influencing the pilgrim's state of acceptance.
